strategyPosture: Index-level calm (SPY 2% off highs, VIX 16.4, credit loose) with real rotation underneath: stay with large-cap momentum, probe — don't chase — the dislocated compounders where revenue growth contradicts price (AVGO, NOW, VST), and keep small-cap duration exposure light while the 10-year sits at 5.24%.

themes.counterRead: The divergence itself is the risk to monitor: if lending standards tighten from 0% or HY OAS widens from 3.12%, the 'rotation' label expires and this becomes the early read of a rollover. For now credit says the equity weakness is selective, not systemic.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 averages 11.54% below 52-week highs vs SPY only 2.0% off — a 9.54-point divergence gap. TSLA is the weakest at -29% while NVDA holds at -2.4%. Against that, bank lending standards read LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.12 — no credit stress corroborating an equity rollover.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — but watch the gap
themes.narrative: The index is fine (SPY +0.37% on the month, 2% from highs) so the market believes breadth is healthy and leadership is merely rotating.
themes.watchFor: Divergence gap widening past -15 points or SLOOS ticking above 10% — either flips the read from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: The market is paying full price for the equipment layer (GEV +9.9% this month, PWR +8.4%, ETN +11.9%) while discounting the fuel and generation names on no new fundamental deterioration — BWXT revenue is growing 18.3%, VST 19.1% with insiders buying $1.17M at the trough. If the AI power thesis is right, the laggard fuel names are mispriced, not broken.
themes.dataAnchor: BWX Technologies sits 43.4% below its high (RSI 32.3) on 18.3% revenue growth; Vistra is 35.6% off its high at 2.7x sales with $1.17M of insider buying at the trough; Cameco fell 11% this month and SMR 15.2%. Meanwhile GEV ripped 3.89% today alone and PWR 3.14%.
themes.label: AI power: equipment repriced, fuel left behind
themes.narrative: AI power demand is the dominant capex theme — equipment and grid names (GEV, PWR, ETN) ripping confirms the market believes the buildout is accelerating.
themes.watchFor: VST or BWXT RSI reclaiming 50 from the low-30s/40s, or any stabilization in uranium pricing — a sentiment turn gaps hardest where positioning is thinnest.

themes.counterRead: The sharpest single divergence in the tape is AVGO: 55% revenue growth, 67.8% gross margins, $26.9B FCF — against a 30.6% drawdown. NOW (+23.1% revenue, -28.6% price) and MDB (-19% in a month on an acute catalyst, fundamentals intact at +22.8% revenue and 71.8% gross margin) rhyme. The caution flag is the template itself: APP (-61.9%) and TTD (-78.5%) carry the same SENTIMENT_DRIVEN label, and at that depth the label is the risk — verify the business before treating either as a dislocation rather than a verdict.
themes.dataAnchor: Eight of the top-conviction names show revenue growing 16-55% YoY while sitting 25-62% below 52-week highs. AVGO: +55% revenue vs -30.6% price. NOW: +23.1% vs -28.6%. MDB dropped 19% in one month with $500M FCF (20.3% margin) intact. RSI readings cluster in the 30s (APP 32, BWXT 32.3, TTD 30.8) — washed out, not basing.
themes.label: Software: the baby and the bathwater
themes.narrative: Enterprise software and AI infrastructure are being sold as a block — the market treats every drawdown in the complex as multiple compression on AI capex doubts.
themes.watchFor: AVGO or NOW printing a higher low with RSI reclaiming 45 — confirmation the fundamental bid is returning; for APP/TTD, any business update before assuming the decline is sentiment.

themes.counterRead: This is a discount for duration, not a distress signal — credit markets (HY OAS 3.12, SLOOS 0%) show no stress that would justify small-cap pricing as fear. The trade is patience: small caps work when the rate regime turns, not before.
themes.dataAnchor: IWM is -3.85% on the month and -7.01% over three months vs SPY +0.37%/+2.39% — persistent, grinding underperformance. The 10-year sits at 5.24% with a real yield of 2.88% and a normally-sloped curve (2s10s +0.35): a higher-for-longer regime that mechanically punishes long-duration small caps.
themes.label: Small caps priced for the rate regime
themes.narrative: Higher-for-longer is keeping small caps pinned — the market believes duration risk stays penalized while the 10-year holds above 5%.
themes.watchFor: IWM 1-month performance turning positive or the 10-year breaking below 5.00% — either signals the duration drag is lifting.

themes.counterRead: The book is barbelled and it is working: META +25.4% this month and BMNR +14% carry the winners' side while NFLX (-15.9% this month, -2.3% today) is the single largest drag. CONL (+7.5%) is leveraged Coinbase — it amplifies the tape in both directions, so size it as the volatility instrument it is.
themes.dataAnchor: Crypto beta ripped into the close: BTC +10.68% and ETH +10.8% on the month, IBIT +9.64%, COIN +7.05% (+1.54% today). Holdings BMNR (+14.04% 1m, +0.83% today) and CONL (+7.45% 1m, +2.96% today) rode it; META (+25.43% 1m) led all large caps. Breakeven inflation sits at 2.36% — no macro headwind to the risk bid today.
themes.label: Crypto beta carrying the book's winners
themes.narrative: Risk-on into the close — crypto and AI-beta names led, and the portfolio's leveraged crypto exposure (BMNR, CONL) captured it.
themes.watchFor: BTC/ETH breaking their monthly highs with volume — continuation signal; or a VIX push above 20, which would argue for trimming the leveraged tail (CONL) first.

watchFor: Mag7/SPY divergence gap widening past -15 points or SLOOS above 10% (rotation becomes rollover)
HY OAS widening past 4.5% (credit stress — currently 3.12%)
IWM 1-month performance turning positive (small-cap regime turn)
VST/BWXT RSI reclaiming 50 from current 30s/40s (nuclear sentiment turn)
Sep CPI (Oct 14) vs 2.36% breakeven — a hot print reprices the whole rate chain
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in the AI power chain: equipment already repriced, so the convexity sits in the laggard fuel and nuclear names (VST, BWXT, CCJ) where a sentiment turn gaps hardest — VST's $1.17M of insider buying at the trough is the sharpest tell in the input. Trigger: uranium price stabilization or a large-cap tech capex guide that re-accelerates the theme.
